question: Name the hill station located on the Nilgiri Hills?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ooty**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Ooty**, officially known as **Udhagamandalam**, is a world-famous hill station located in the **Nilgiri Hills** of **Tamil Nadu**, **India**. It is situated at an elevation of approximately **2,240 meters** above sea level and serves as the administrative headquarters of the **Nilgiris district**. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***

• **Shimla** is the capital city of **Himachal Pradesh** and is situated in the **Himalayan** foothills. It is not located in the Nilgiri range of South India. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

• **Darjeeling** is a town in the state of **West Bengal**, located in the **Lesser Himalayas**. It is globally renowned for its tea industry and the **Darjeeling Himalayan Railway**. It is not part of the Nilgiri Hills. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

• **Manali** is a popular resort town in the **Beas River** valley of **Himachal Pradesh**. It is located in the **Himalayas** and serves as a gateway to the **Lahaul and Spiti district**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Nilgiri Hills** are a range of mountains forming part of the **Western Ghats** in northwestern **Tamil Nadu**, **Karnataka**, and **Kerala**.

• The highest point in the Nilgiris is **Doddabetta Peak**, which stands at an elevation of **2,637 meters**.

• The **Nilgiri Mountain Railway**, connecting **Mettupalayam** to **Ooty**, was declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **2005**.

• The region is famous for the **Neelakurinji** flower, which blooms once every **12 years**, covering the hills in a bluish hue and giving them the name **'Blue Mountains'**.

• The **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve** was the first biosphere reserve in India, established in **September 1986** by **UNESCO**.

**Important Points__**

• The **Nilgiris** are separated from the **Karnataka Plateau** to the north by the **Moyar River** and from the **Anaimalai Hills** to the south by the **Palakkad Gap**.

• The area is home to several protected regions, including **Mudumalai National Park**, **Mukurthi National Park**, and **Bandipur National Park**.

• The indigenous people of the Nilgiris include tribes such as the **Toda people**, who are known for their distinct culture, traditional barrel-shaped huts, and dairy-based economy.

• The local economy is heavily dependent on **tourism** and **agriculture**, specifically the cultivation of **tea**, **coffee**, and **eucalyptus**.
